steps.note: Create the trigger function that copies customer_id into the new bigint column on every insert/update. Touches no table.
steps.sql: CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.orders_customer_id_sync() RETURNS trigger LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $f$ BEGIN NEW.customer_id_new := NEW.customer_id; RETURN NEW; END $f$;

steps.note: In one short transaction, retried with a 300ms lock_timeout so app queries never queue behind it for long: add the nullable bigint column customer_id_new (metadata-only, no rewrite), a NOT VALID check that it is not null (enforced for new rows only), and the sync trigger. From here on every new order fills both columns.
steps.sql: DO $$ BEGIN FOR i IN 1..100 LOOP BEGIN PERFORM set_config('lock_timeout', '300ms', true); LOCK TABLE public.orders IN ACCESS EXCLUSIVE MODE; ALTER TABLE public.orders ADD COLUMN customer_id_new bigint; ALTER TABLE public.orders ADD CONSTRAINT orders_customer_id_new_chk CHECK (customer_id_new IS NOT NULL) NOT VALID; CREATE TRIGGER orders_customer_id_sync BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE ON public.orders FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION public.orders_customer_id_sync(); RETURN; EXCEPTION WHEN lock_not_available THEN PERFORM pg_sleep(0.5); END; END LOOP; RAISE EXCEPTION 'could not lock orders to add customer_id_new'; END $$;

steps.note: Verify before touching the live column: every row must have customer_id_new equal to customer_id. Fails the plan (nothing swapped yet, app unaffected) if any row differs.
steps.sql: SET statement_timeout = 0; DO $$ BEGIN IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.orders WHERE customer_id_new IS DISTINCT FROM customer_id) THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'customer_id_new does not match customer_id on some rows'; END IF; END $$;

steps.note: Validate the not-null check over all rows. Takes only a SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE lock, so reads and writes continue.
steps.sql: SET statement_timeout = 0; ALTER TABLE public.orders VALIDATE CONSTRAINT orders_customer_id_new_chk;

steps.note: Collect planner statistics for the new column (they stay with it through the rename), so the /customer query keeps its current plan.
steps.sql: SET statement_timeout = 0; ANALYZE public.orders;

steps.note: Swap in one short transaction, retried with a 300ms lock_timeout: SET NOT NULL on customer_id_new (no scan, proven by the validated check), drop the check and the trigger, drop the old integer column (metadata-only, no rewrite), rename customer_id_new to customer_id. The app's SQL is unchanged and uses the bigint column from its next query.
steps.sql: DO $$ BEGIN FOR i IN 1..100 LOOP BEGIN PERFORM set_config('lock_timeout', '300ms', true); LOCK TABLE public.orders IN ACCESS EXCLUSIVE MODE; ALTER TABLE public.orders ALTER COLUMN customer_id_new SET NOT NULL; ALTER TABLE public.orders DROP CONSTRAINT orders_customer_id_new_chk; DROP TRIGGER orders_customer_id_sync ON public.orders; ALTER TABLE public.orders DROP COLUMN customer_id; ALTER TABLE public.orders RENAME COLUMN customer_id_new TO customer_id; RETURN; EXCEPTION WHEN lock_not_available THEN PERFORM pg_sleep(0.5); END; END LOOP; RAISE EXCEPTION 'could not lock orders to swap customer_id'; END $$;

steps.note: Drop the now unused trigger function and check the result: orders.customer_id is bigint NOT NULL.
steps.sql: DROP FUNCTION public.orders_customer_id_sync(); DO $$ BEGIN IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema = 'public' AND table_name = 'orders' AND column_name = 'customer_id' AND data_type = 'bigint' AND is_nullable = 'NO') THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'orders.customer_id is not bigint NOT NULL'; END IF; END $$;
